outcomeNote: A single dictum with its prooftext; the opening ואמר marks it as the paired sequel to R' Avin HaLevi's ruling for the living (לך לשלום) in the preceding unit.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: הַנִּפְטָר מִן הַמֵּת אַל יֹאמַר לוֹ ״לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם״, אֶלָּא ״לֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאַתָּה תָּבוֹא אֶל אֲבֹתֶיךָ בְּשָׁלוֹם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Avin HaLevi also said: One who takes leave from a dead person should not say to him: Go to peace, but rather,» one should say: «Go in peace, as it is stated: “But you shall go to your fathers in peace”» (Genesis 15:15).

moves.summary: R' Avin HaLevi rules that one taking leave of the dead says 'go in peace', not 'go to peace'
moves.about: prooftext that one takes leave of the dead with 'go in peace' (בשלום), not 'go to peace'

moves.summary: proves it from Genesis 15:15, which says of Abraham's death 'you shall go to your fathers in peace (בשלום)'
